analysis.title: Europe Healthcare: Sector check in: Monitoring sector valuation, earnings execution and innovation momentum
key_insights: 3Q26 European BioPharma reporting showed 60% of companies beating revenue consensus and 86% beating earnings consensus, versus 64%/91% in 2Q26 and 40%/70% in 1Q26. GSK has met or beaten both revenue and earnings consensus at every report since 1Q24.
Post-3Q26 consensus FY26 revenue revisions average +2% and EPS revisions +3%. GS forecasts show the most upside risk versus consensus for UCB and Sanofi across 2026-2028.

FX guidance improved for Galderma, GSK, Novo Nordisk, Roche and Sanofi. Roche, GSK, Sanofi and Novo guide to an average -1.5% revenue and -3% earnings FX impact for 2026, versus -2%/-3% on revenue and -4% on earnings at 2Q/1Q26. Roche's 3% turnover drag implies a 5% hit to core operating profit and EPS.

Clinical execution has moderated. Sector Phase 3 success is 60% YTD 2026 versus 82% at 1Q26 and 75% at 2Q26 and 71% in FY25. Trailing 12 month delivery is 55%, down from 69% at 2Q26. NME readouts YTD: eight positive, nine negative, two mixed across 19.

AstraZeneca is named innovation leader on the absolute number of positive readouts and approvals, success rate on >$500mn assets, and count of first/best-in-class assets. Argenx, AstraZeneca and Roche beat the sector-average YTD Phase 3 success rate among companies with more than one readout.

Valuation and clinical delivery have diverged. AstraZeneca's 12-month Phase 3 delivery is 55% and the stock is -7% over 12 months (16.3x versus 17.6x). Novartis is +14% (17.7x versus 15.5x) despite a 50% delivery rate.

EU large cap pharma trades at 13.6x 12-month forward P/E, a 3% discount to SXXP. The discount was 13% in August and 10% in May 2026. The sector has averaged about a 1% premium over 25 years. US large cap pharma trades at 20.7x, about a 54% premium to EU, versus a 9% 10-year average premium.

GS stays cautious on the sector given the loss-of-exclusivity cliff, mixed clinical delivery and modest near-term earnings growth. Average annual LoE drag is about 2% over FY26-30, with Novartis most affected and Sanofi most affected in the 2030s.
Ratings: Buy on AstraZeneca, Bayer, Argenx (on the Conviction List), Galderma, UCB and Sandoz. Sell on Novartis. Neutral on GSK, Novo Nordisk, Roche and Sanofi.

M&A capacity at 3x EBITDA is about $600bn for large cap pharma. Novartis has the most deals YTD (seven) and GSK leads on value (c.$15.8bn cumulative), including Nuvalent at $10.6bn upfront. Oncology (30%) and immunology (27%) lead deal activity, with growing access to China-originated assets and AI-linked partnerships.

Argenx: the December Phase 3 readout of empasiprubart in MMN is the key catalyst. GS sees Phase 2 ARDA data and trial design as supportive but flags risk from the small dataset and uncertain IVIg-comparable efficacy.

AstraZeneca: AVANZAR readout is delayed to 1Q27 and GS models a 40% probability of success. GS supports the $80bn 2030 revenue target and sees roughly $20bn of potential revenue de-risked through 2027.

Bayer: a court ruling on the glyphosate settlement is expected before Christmas. A successful approval could largely contain further litigation provisions. GS sees the Pharma business as under-appreciated.

Novartis: GS sees a structural growth reset from generic headwinds. Shares are up c.20% since Sept 9th, which GS attributes to market moves and a faster buyback, and calls the outperformance unjustified ahead of LoE waves. Meet the Management event on 18-19 Nov is the focus.

Roche: GS is below consensus on 2027 giredestrant sales at CHF400m versus company consensus CHF638m, citing the patient assistance programme and a steady launch. Shares trade at 17.4x 2027E EPS, about a 20% premium to the sector, with headline risk from EMBER-4 and CAMBRIA-1.

Sanofi trades at 8.8x 2027E EPS, a 55% discount to the sector. Investors are waiting for clarity on strategic direction. Much of the c.5% earnings upside beyond 2026 comes from Dupixent, which deepens the post-2031 patent cliff.
Sandoz: more than $275bn of biosimilar LoE value (US and EU) across 2026-36 supports a Buy. Watch Enzeevu US launch, GLP-1 generics in Brazil and Canada, and the FY27 guide.

UCB: GS sees the Bimzelx growth opportunity intact and views the guidance upgrade as a positive. The lutikizumab overhang is removed after INTREPID, and the remibrutinib Phase 3 readout is the remaining competitor risk.
Novo Nordisk: GS expects c.1% CER growth in 2027 and c.2% operating profit growth, with faster growth from 2028. Catalysts include CagriSema REDEFINE-11 in 1H27 and cagrilintide RENEW1&2 in 2H27.
GSK: GS stays Neutral on limited pipeline optionality and modest launches of Exdensur and Blenrep, and sees risk to the >£40bn 2031 revenue guidance.

market_movers.rationale: Best mix of growth and pipeline optionality, with valuation seen as increasingly attractive and multiple catalysts through 2027.
A potential court ruling on the glyphosate settlement before Christmas and under-appreciated Pharma growth. GS cites asymmetric risk-reward.
On the European Conviction List. Outsized growth and pipeline optionality ahead of the December empasiprubart MMN Phase 3 readout.
Galderma growth and margin expansion seen as best-in-class on the Nemluvio ramp, with scarcity value supporting the valuation.
UCB's Bimzelx growth intact on head-to-head superiority, with guidance upgraded and the lutikizumab overhang removed.
Sandoz is well placed for the biosimilar loss-of-exclusivity decade, with over $275bn of LoE value across 2026-36.
Generic headwinds and patent expirations are weighing on earnings momentum. The stock trades at a premium to the sector with downside seen as under-reflected.
Limited pipeline optionality and modest Exdensur and Blenrep launches, despite a re-rating since 2025.
Key debates are the ex-US Wegovy pill launch and the ability to grow earnings in 2027.
A premium multiple, shares near all-time highs and 2027 risks from the giredestrant launch and competitor readouts.
Strategic direction uncertainty keeps investors on the sidelines despite an 8.8x 2027E P/E.

sector_views.rationale: GS is cautious at the sector level on the upcoming LoE cliff, mixed clinical delivery and modest near-term earnings growth, though the sector trades at a discount to its own history.
Double-digit market growth and over $275bn of LoE value across 2026-36 favour Sandoz.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 sector tracker: 60% of European BioPharma companies beat revenue consensus and 86% beat earnings consensus (reported results versus consensus), versus 64%/91% at 2Q26 and 27%/73% at 4Q25.
Since 1Q25, companies beat both consensus revenue and earnings on c.49% of occasions where both estimates were available.

3Q26 results versus consensus: Sanofi revenue +9%, operating profit +26%, EPS +26%. Novo Nordisk revenue +8%, operating profit +12%, EPS +14%. AstraZeneca revenue +2%, operating profit +9%, EPS +8%. Argenx revenue +7% beat and operating profit -9% miss (19% beat excluding one-off SG&A).
Bayer 3Q26: revenue in line (+1%), EBITDA pre-special items +13% versus consensus, but EPS missed by 14%. Guidance raised on sales and EBITDA pre-special items.
Sandoz 3Q26 sales update missed consensus by 2% and narrowed sales guidance to the bottom end while raising core EBITDA margin guidance.
Post-3Q26 FY26 consensus revisions: Novo revenue +7% and EPS +12%. Novartis core EPS -5% despite revenue +1% and core operating profit +4%. Sanofi sales +5% and EPS +5%.
Share price move since results: Bayer +8%, Sanofi +8%, Argenx +10%, Novo -5%, GSK +1%. On the day: AstraZeneca +7%, Novo +6%, Sanofi +5%, GSK -5%.
risk_factors: Loss-of-exclusivity cliff: average annual drag of about 2% on sector growth in FY26-30, rising in the 2030s.
Declining clinical delivery: sector Phase 3 success at 60% YTD and trailing 12 month delivery at 55%.
Argenx empasiprubart Phase 3 MMN readout in December carries risk given the small Phase 2 dataset.
AstraZeneca AVANZAR is a multi-year overhang ahead of the 1Q27 readout.
Bayer glyphosate settlement approval is uncertain and Crop Science performance into next year is a concern.
Roche giredestrant launch risk and headline risk from EMBER-4 (LLY) and CAMBRIA-1 (AZN) readouts.
US pharma tariffs and MFN pricing policy.
Sanofi Regeneron payaway and FX-driven downward EPS revisions.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows EU pharma trading at a 3% discount to SXXP on 12-month forward P/E, with the discount at 13% in August and 10% in May 2026.
Exhibit 14 compares 12-month trailing Phase 3 delivery rates by company, Nov 2026 versus 2Q26, with Roche at 80% and Novo Nordisk and Sanofi at 33%.
vol_and_positioning: Novartis buyback pace rose from 130k to 400k shares per day since Sept 10th. At that rate GS estimates the current programme completes in Feb 2027.
Novartis shares are close to all-time highs and Roche shares are near all-time highs, while Sanofi trades at a 55% discount to the sector on 2027E P/E.
geopolitical: US pharma tariffs and Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) pricing policy are cited as a risk to UCB.

tension_points.bull_case: AstraZeneca has the most Phase 3 successes in absolute terms, best-in-class growth and pipeline mix, and a valuation GS sees as increasingly attractive with several 2027 catalysts.
tension_points.bear_case: AstraZeneca's 12-month Phase 3 delivery is 55% and the stock is -7% over 12 months, while Novartis rose 14% on a lower 50% delivery rate, so clinical delivery and stock performance have diverged. The AVANZAR readout is a multi-year overhang.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A negative AVANZAR outcome at the 1Q27 readout, for which GS models a 40% probability of success.

tension_points.bull_case: The stock is near all-time highs on market strength and an accelerated buyback, and GS sees the catalyst path as less risky from here.
tension_points.bear_case: GS sees a structural growth reset from generic headwinds and the outperformance as unjustified ahead of significant waves of LoEs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Clearer stepping stones behind the longer-term mid single-digit growth guide and stronger sales from key franchises, which GS lists as upside risks to the Sell.

tension_points.bull_case: Phase 2 ARDA data, the Phase 3 trial design, GS statistical simulations and physician feedback support a positive outcome.
tension_points.bear_case: The Phase 2 dataset is small, IVIg-comparable efficacy is uncertain, and rare-disease Phase 2 results do not always translate into Phase 3.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A negative or weak December Phase 3 EMPASSION readout in MMN.

tension_points.bull_case: Management expects court approval of the settlement before Christmas, which could largely contain further glyphosate litigation provisions, alongside strong Pharma performance.
tension_points.bear_case: Litigation will dominate sentiment near term and investors worry about Crop performance into next year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The court failing to approve the glyphosate settlement before Christmas.

theme_stances.evidence: AstraZeneca remains the innovation leader in the sector

theme_stances.key_argument: The biosimilar market should keep growing at double digits on a wave of loss of exclusivity.
theme_stances.evidence: The biosimilar market is expected to continue on a double-digit growth trajectory
